items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-05-26
items.q: Russell Roberts says to me... that's Hannity's tune... I said, let me go and see him. I may be able to record it for him... I recorded the number.

ctx.x: Sure. Well, nobody will hear this, ya know. We can save it, ya know. And, uh, put it down. Right. Put it down. Right. Put it down.

By blowing the cornet, I was making this. Da, And by forcing, the back part would go. You understand what I mean? I see. And that gave me an idea of putting that into the throat. And I tried to make that on the horn, and I made it on the horn. On the horn. See, on this cornet. Not this one. The one that I had was a little bit. A piece of junk. Now, that's the whole tiger rag in completion. It has a little part of the quadrill. And if anyone says they have it in there, you play the tiger, if you played the tiger…

He wouldn't even play jazz or the blues. He'd committed to paper. This Negro here had went into the hands of the receiver. And I know this tune by the name of Jobo Blues. And I used to play it in the band. And Russell Roberts says to me, you know whose tune that is? I said, no. He says, that's Hannity's tune. I says, it's a damn good tune. I said, let me go and see him. I may be able to record it for him. At that time, he was in the hands of the receiver. I went on over there. And he wasn't there. I spoke to his…
